q: Did the Red Sox or the Yankees have better season opener attendance in 2024?
title: Red Sox and Yankees opening game attendance, 2024
cited: The New York Yankees had better home opener attendance than the Boston Red Sox in 2024 (table: games). The New York Yankees' 2024 home opener (on April 5, 2024) had an attendance of 47,812 fans and 102.7% of listed capacity (table: games; query: Q2). The Boston Red Sox's 2024 home opener (on April 9, 2024) had an attendance of 36,093 fans and 95.6% of capacity (table: games; query: Q2). The difference in attendance between the two teams' home openers (Yankees minus Red Sox) was 11,719 fans (table: games; query: Q2). The difference in fill rate between the two teams' home openers (Yankees minus Red Sox) was approximately 7.1 percentage points (table: games; query: Q2). The database does not contain separate records for "season opener" (first game of the entire MLB season) versus "home opener" for these specific teams beyond their home openers, and queries were limited (table: games).

The difference in fill rate between the two teams' home openers (Yankees minus Red Sox) was approximately 7.1 percentage points[2]. SELECT g1.home_team AS red_sox_game_team, g1.away_team AS red_sox_away_team, g1.attendance AS red_sox_attendance, g1.fill_rate AS red_sox_fill_rate, g2.home_team AS yankees_game_team, g2.away_team AS yankees_away_team, g2.attendance AS yankees_attendance, g2.fill_rate AS yankees_fill_rate, g1.attendance - g2.attendance AS attendance_difference, g1.fill_rate - g2.fill_rate AS fill_rate_difference FROM games g1, games g2 WHERE g1.game_pk = 745283 AND g2.game_pk = 746418

q: Compare actual and expected average attendance for the five AL East teams in 2025.

chart.title: Actual and expected attendance by team

title: AL East actual vs expected attendance, 2025

check_failures.message: The data shows what went together, not causes: remove the stated cause.

chart.title: Average attendance by month, 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026

title: Dodgers attendance, 2024 to 2026
cited: The Dodgers averaged 49,805 fans per game in 2026, which was below the predicted 50,414 fans but represented a 0.5% increase from the season before, continuing a three-year growth trend (table: team_season_model, team_season_attendance; query: Q2). In 2024, the team averaged 48,657 fans per game (totaling 3,941,251), which was below the predicted 50,550 fans but was a 2.7% increase from the prior year while drawing 87.6% of capacity during a 98-64 season (table: team_season_model, team_season_attendance, games_clean; query: Q2). In 2025, the Dodgers went 93-69 and averaged 49,537 fans (totaling 4,012,470), which was above the predicted 48,078 fans, up 1.8% year-over-year, and drew 88.5% of capacity (table: team_season_model, team_season_attendance, games_clean; query: Q2). The 2026 season saw the team finish 100-62, totaling 4,034,219 home fans and drawing 88.9% of capacity (table: team_season_attendance, games_clean; query: Q2).

sources.query: SELECT tsm.season, tsm.official_home_total, tsm.avg_attendance, tsm.expected_avg_attendance, tsm.record, tsm.yoy_change_pct, tsa.home_average, tsa.home_total, AVG(g.fill_pct) AS avg_fill_pct FROM team_season_model tsm JOIN team_season_attendance tsa ON tsm.team_id = tsa.team_id AND tsm.season = tsa.season LEFT JOIN games_clean g ON g.home_team_id = tsm.team_id AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM g.official_date) = tsm.season WHERE tsm.team_id = 119 GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 ORDER BY tsm.season
